translation_en: Ali ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, who heard Urwah. Abu Humayd al-Saidi informed us that the Prophet appointed a man from Banu Asad, called Ibn al-Utabiyyah, to collect charity. When he returned, he said, “This is for you, and this was given to me as a gift.” The Prophet stood on the pulpit (Sufyan also said that he ascended the pulpit), praised and glorified Allah, then said: “What is wrong with an official whom we send out, then he comes back saying, ‘This is for you and this is for me’? Why did he not sit in his father’s and mother’s house and see whether he would be given a gift or not? By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, he will not bring anything without bringing it on the Day of Resurrection, carrying it on his neck: if it is a camel, it will groan; if a cow, it will bellow; and if a sheep, it will bleat.” Then he raised his hands until we saw the whiteness of his armpits and said three times: “Have I conveyed the message?” Sufyan said: Al-Zuhri related it to us. Hisham added, from his father, from Abu Humayd: “My ears heard it and my eyes saw him; ask Zayd ibn Thabit, for he heard it with me.” Al-Zuhri did not say, “My ears heard it.” “Bellow” is a sound; the groaning mentioned in “you cry out” is like the sound of a cow.

Uthman ibn Salih narrated to us; Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us; Ibn Jurayj informed me that Nafi informed him that Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, told him: Salim, the freedman of Abu Hudhayfah, used to lead the first Emigrants and the Companions of the Prophet in prayer at the mosque of Quba. Among them were Abu Bakr, Umar, Abu Salamah, Zayd, and Amir ibn Rabi’ah.

Ismail ibn Abi Uways narrated to us; Ismail ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, from his uncle Musa ibn Uqbah. Ibn Shihab said: Urwah ibn al-Zubayr told me that Marwan ibn al-Hakam and al-Miswar ibn Makhramah informed him that when the Muslims had permitted the captives of Hawazin to be freed, the Messenger of Allah said: “I do not know which of you gave permission and which did not. Return until your leaders bring your decision to us.” The people returned, and their leaders spoke with them. Then they returned to the Messenger of Allah and told him that the people had willingly consented and given permission.

Abu Nuaym narrated to us; Asim ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn Abdullah ibn Umar narrated to us, from his father, who said: Some people said to Ibn Umar, “We enter upon our rulers and tell them something different from what we say when we leave them.” He said, “We used to regard that as hypocrisy.”

Qutaybah narrated to us; al-Layth narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Iraq, from Abu Hurayrah, who heard the Messenger of Allah say: “The worst of people is the two-faced person, who comes to these people with one face and to those people with another.”

Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us; Sufyan informed us, from Hisham, from his father, from Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her: Hind said to the Prophet, “Abu Sufyan is a stingy man, and I need to take from his property.” He said: “Take what is sufficient for you and your children, in a reasonable manner.”

Abd al-Aziz ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Ibrahim ibn Sad narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that Zaynab, daughter of Abu Salamah, told him that Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet, told her that the Messenger of Allah heard a dispute at the door of his chamber. He came out to them and said: “I am only a human being. People bring their disputes to me, and perhaps one of you is more persuasive than another, so I may think that he is truthful and rule in his favor. If I rule in favor of someone concerning a Muslim’s right, it is only a piece of the Fire; let him take it or leave it.”

Ismail narrated to us; he said: Malik narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Aishah, the wife of the Prophet, who said: Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas instructed his brother Sad ibn Abi Waqqas, saying, “The son of Zamah’s slave woman is my son, so take him into your custody.” In the year of the Conquest, Sad took him and said, “He is my brother; my brother instructed me concerning him.” Abd ibn Zamah stood up and said, “He is my brother and the son of my father’s slave woman; he was born on his bed.” They went together to the Messenger of Allah. Sad said, “Messenger of Allah, he is my brother; my brother instructed me concerning him.” Abd ibn Zamah said, “He is my brother and the son of my father’s slave woman; he was born on his bed.” The Messenger of Allah said: “He is yours, Abd ibn Zamah.” Then he said: “The child belongs to the bed, and the adulterer gets the stone.” Then he said to Sawdah bint Zamah, “Veil yourself from him,” because he saw that he resembled Utbah. She never saw him again until she died.

Ishaq ibn Nasr narrated to us; Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us; Sufyan informed us, from Mansur and al-Amash, from Abu Wa’il, who said: Abdullah said that the Prophet said: “Whoever swears a binding oath, while lying in it, in order to seize property, will meet Allah while He is angry with him.” Then Allah revealed: “Indeed, those who exchange Allah’s covenant...” (3:77). Al-Ashath came while Abdullah was relating this to them and said, “It was revealed about me and a man with whom I disputed over a well.” The Prophet said: “Do you have proof?” I said, “No.” He said: “Then let him swear.” I said, “Then he will swear.” So the verse, “Indeed, those who exchange Allah’s covenant...” was revealed.

Abu al-Yaman narrated to us; Shuaib informed us, from al-Zuhri. Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that Zaynab bint Abu Salamah told him, from her mother Umm Salamah, who said: The Prophet heard the noise of people disputing at his door. He came out to them and said: “I am only a human being. People bring their disputes to me, and perhaps one of them is more persuasive than another, so I rule in his favor thinking he is truthful. If I rule in favor of someone concerning a Muslim’s right, it is only a piece of the Fire; let him take it or leave it.”

Ibn Numayr narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us; Ismail narrated to us; Salamah ibn Kuhayl narrated to us, from Ata, from Jabir, who said: The Prophet was told that one of his Companions had freed a slave after his death, and that he had no property other than that slave. The Prophet sold him for 800 dirhams, then sent the price to the man.

Musa ibn Ismail narrated to us; Abd al-Aziz ibn Muslim narrated to us; Abdullah ibn Dinar narrated to us, who said: I heard Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, say: The Messenger of Allah sent out an expedition and appointed Usamah ibn Zayd over them. People criticized his appointment. He said: “If you criticize his appointment, you previously criticized the appointment of his father. By Allah, he was worthy of leadership and was among the people most beloved to me; and this one is among the people most beloved to me after him.”

Musaddad narrated to us; Yahya ibn Said narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I heard Ibn Abi Mulaykah narrate from Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: “The man most hated by Allah is the stubborn adversary.”

Mahmud narrated to us; Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us; Mamar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from Ibn Umar. The Prophet sent Khalid out. (Another chain:) Nuaym narrated to me; Abdullah informed us; Mamar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, who said: The Prophet sent Khalid ibn al-Walid to Banu Jadhimah. They did not know how to say, “We have accepted Islam,” so they said, “We have become Sabians.” Khalid began killing and taking captives, and gave each of us a captive. Then he ordered each of us to kill his captive. I said, “By Allah, I will not kill my captive, and none of my companions will kill his captive.” We told the Prophet about this, and he said twice: “O Allah, I disavow to You what Khalid ibn al-Walid did.”

Abu al-Numan narrated to us; Hammad narrated to us; Abu Hazim al-Madani narrated to us, from Sahl ibn Sad al-Saidi, who said: Fighting broke out between Banu Amr, and the Prophet was informed. He prayed the noon prayer, then went to them to make peace. When the afternoon prayer time came, Bilal gave the call to prayer and the call to begin it, and the Prophet ordered Abu Bakr to lead. The Prophet arrived while Abu Bakr was praying and made his way through the people until he stood behind Abu Bakr, in the row next to him. The people clapped. Abu Bakr did not usually turn around during prayer, but when the clapping continued, he looked and saw the Prophet behind him. The Prophet gestured to him to continue and gestured with his hand. Abu Bakr remained a little while praising Allah for the Prophet’s instruction, then stepped backward. The Prophet moved forward and led the prayer. When he finished, he said: “O Abu Bakr, what prevented you from continuing to lead when I instructed you to?” Abu Bakr said: “It was not fitting for the son of Abu Quhafah to lead the Messenger of Allah.” The Prophet said: “Why did I see you clapping so much? If something happens to you in prayer, men should say ‘Glory be to Allah’; women should clap.”

Muhammad ibn Ubaydullah Abu Thabit narrated to us; Ibrahim ibn Sad narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Ubayd ibn al-Sabbaq, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: After the people of Yamama were killed, Abu Bakr sent for me while Umar was with him. Abu Bakr said: “Umar came to me and said, ‘The killing of the Quran reciters was severe on the day of Yamama, and I fear that the killing of Quran reciters may become severe in other battles too, so that much of the Quran may be lost. I think you should order that the Quran be collected.’ I said to Umar, ‘How can I do something that the Messenger of Allah did not do?’ Umar said, ‘By Allah, it is good.’ Umar kept urging me until Allah opened my heart to what He had opened Umar’s heart to, and I came to share Umar’s view.” Zayd said: Abu Bakr said to me, “You are a young, intelligent man, and we do not suspect you. You used to write the revelation for the Messenger of Allah. So seek out the Quran and collect it.” By Allah, if they had charged me with moving a mountain, it would not have been harder for me than what he ordered me to do: collect the Quran. I said, “How can you do something the Messenger of Allah did not do?” He said, “By Allah, it is good.” Abu Bakr kept urging me until Allah opened my heart as He had opened theirs. I sought out the Quran and collected it from palm stalks, thin stones, and the memories of men. I found the end of Surat al-Tawbah with Abu Khuzaymah al-Ansari, and I did not find it with anyone else: “There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves... (Quran 9:128–129)” through the end of the surah. The collected sheets remained with Abu Bakr until Allah took him, then with Umar during his life, then with Hafsah bint Umar. (A lakhaf is a pottery shard.)

Abdullah ibn Yusuf narrated to us; Malik informed us, from Abu Layla. (Another chain:) Ismail narrated to us; Malik narrated to me, from Abu Layla ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Sahl, from Sahl ibn Abi Hathmah, who told him, along with men from the elders of his people: Abdullah ibn Sahl and Muhayyisah went to Khaybar because hardship had befallen them. Muhayyisah was told that Abdullah had been killed and thrown into a shallow well or spring. He went to the Jews and said, “By Allah, you killed him.” They replied, “By Allah, we did not kill him.” He returned to his people and told them. Then he came with his brother Huwayyisah, who was older than him, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Sahl. Muhayyisah began to speak, as he had been at Khaybar, but the Prophet said to him, “Let the older one speak first.” Huwayyisah spoke, then Muhayyisah. The Messenger of Allah said: “Either they pay blood money for your companion, or they declare war.” The Messenger of Allah wrote to them, and they replied in writing, “We did not kill him.” The Messenger of Allah said to Huwayyisah, Muhayyisah, and Abd al-Rahman: “Will you swear and thereby claim the blood of your companion?” They said, “No.” He said: “Then will the Jews swear for you?” They said, “They are not Muslims.” So the Messenger of Allah paid one hundred camels from his own property, and they were brought into the house. Sahl said: One of those camels kicked me.

Adam narrated to us; Ibn Abi Dhib narrated to us; al-Zuhri narrated to us, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah, from Abu Hurayrah and Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani, who said: A Bedouin came and said, “Messenger of Allah, judge between us according to the Book of Allah.” His opponent stood and said, “He is right; judge between us according to the Book of Allah.” The Bedouin said, “My son worked for this man, then committed adultery with his wife. They told me that my son must be stoned, so I ransomed him from that with one hundred sheep and a slave girl. Then I asked the people of knowledge, and they told me that my son must receive one hundred lashes and be exiled for one year.” The Prophet said: “I will judge between you according to the Book of Allah. The slave girl and sheep are to be returned to you, and your son must receive one hundred lashes and be exiled for one year. And you, Unays”—he said this to a man—“go to this man’s wife tomorrow morning and stone her.” Unays went to her the next morning and stoned her.

Kharijah ibn Zayd ibn Thabit reported from Zayd ibn Thabit that the Prophet ordered him to learn the writing of the Jews. He said: “I wrote the Prophet’s letters for him, and I read their letters to him when they wrote to him.” Umar said, while Ali, Abd al-Rahman, and Uthman were with him, “What does this say?” Abd al-Rahman ibn Hatib replied, “It tells you what their associate did to the two of them.” Abu Jamrah said: “I used to interpret between Ibn Abbas and the people.” Some people said that a judge must have two interpreters.

Abu al-Yaman narrated to us; Shuaib informed us, from al-Zuhri. Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah informed me that Abdullah ibn Abbas told him that Abu Sufyan ibn Harb informed him: Heraclius sent for him among a caravan of Quraysh. Then he said to his interpreter, “Tell them: I am going to question this man. If he lies to me, call him a liar.” (Abu Sufyan then recounted the hadith.) Heraclius said to his interpreter: “Tell him: If what you say is true, he will rule the place where these two feet of mine stand.”

Muhammad narrated to us; Abdah informed us; Hisham ibn Urwah narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Humayd al-Saidi: The Prophet appointed Ibn al-Utabiyyah to collect the charity of Banu Sulaym. When he came to the Messenger of Allah and gave his account, he said, “This is what is for you, and this is a gift given to me.” The Messenger of Allah said: “Why did you not sit in your father’s house and your mother’s house until your gift came to you, if you are truthful?” Then the Messenger of Allah stood, addressed the people, praised and glorified Allah, and said: “To proceed: I appoint men from among you over matters Allah has entrusted to me. One of you comes and says, ‘This is for you, and this is a gift given to me.’ Why did he not sit in his father’s house and his mother’s house until his gift came to him, if he is truthful? By Allah, none of you will take anything from it unlawfully without coming on the Day of Resurrection carrying it. Let me not find one of you coming to Allah carrying a camel that groans, a cow that bellows, or a sheep that bleats.” Then he raised his hands until I saw the whiteness of his armpits and said: “Have I conveyed the message?”

Asbagh narrated to us; Ibn Wahb informed us; Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Said al-Khudri, from the Prophet, who said: “Allah did not send any prophet or appoint any successor without that person having two close advisers: one who urges him to do good and encourages him in it, and one who urges him to do evil and encourages him in it. The one protected is the one Allah protects.” Sulayman reported this from Yahya, from Ibn Shihab; Ibn Abi Atiq and Musa also reported the same from Ibn Shihab. Shuaib reported it from al-Zuhri, who said that Abu Salamah narrated it from Abu Said as his own statement. Al-Awzai and Muawiyah ibn Sallam reported it from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet. Ibn Abi Husayn and Said ibn Ziyad reported it from Abu Salamah, from Abu Said as his own statement. Ubaydullah ibn Abi Jafar reported: Safwan narrated to me, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Ayyub, who said, “I heard the Prophet.”

Ismail narrated to me; Malik narrated to me, from Yahya ibn Said, who said: Ubadah ibn al-Walid informed me; my father informed me, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: We pledged to the Messenger of Allah to listen and obey in ease and hardship, not to dispute authority with those entitled to it, and to stand—or speak—for the truth wherever we were, not fearing the blame of anyone for Allah’s sake.

Amr ibn Ali narrated to us; Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us; Humayd narrated to us, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him: The Prophet came out on a cold morning while the Emigrants and the Ansar were digging the trench. He said: “O Allah, the true good is the good of the Hereafter, so forgive the Ansar and the Emigrants.” They replied: “We are those who pledged to Muhammad to strive in jihad for as long as we live.”

Abdullah ibn Yusuf narrated to us; Malik informed us, from Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: When we pledged to the Messenger of Allah to listen and obey, he would say to us: “As far as you are able.”

Musaddad narrated to us; Yahya narrated to us, from Sufyan; Abdullah ibn Dinar narrated to us, who said: I was present when the people gathered around Abd al-Malik. Ibn Umar wrote: “I acknowledge listening and obedience to Abd al-Malik, Commander of the Faithful, according to the Sunnah of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger, as far as I am able. My sons have acknowledged the same.”

Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us; Hushaym narrated to us; Sayyar informed us, from al-Shabi, from Jarir ibn Abdullah, who said: I pledged to the Prophet to listen and obey. He instructed me to add, “as far as you are able,” and to give sincere counsel to every Muslim.

Amr ibn Ali narrated to us; Yahya narrated to us, from Sufyan, who said: Abdullah ibn Dinar narrated to me. He said: When the people pledged allegiance to Abd al-Malik, Abdullah ibn Umar wrote to him: “To Abdullah Abd al-Malik, Commander of the Faithful: I acknowledge listening and obedience to you, according to the Sunnah of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger, as far as I am able. My sons have acknowledged this as well.”
Abdullah ibn Maslamah narrated to us; Hatim narrated to us, from Yazid, who said: I asked Salamah, “What did you pledge to the Prophet on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah?” He said, “We pledged to die.”

Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Asma narrated to us; Juwayriyah narrated to us, from Malik, from al-Zuhri, that Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman informed him that al-Miswar ibn Makhramah informed him: The group whom Umar had appointed gathered and consulted one another. Abd al-Rahman said to them, “I am not competing with you for this matter, but if you wish, I will choose one of you for you.” They entrusted the decision to Abd al-Rahman. When they put him in charge of their affair, people gathered around him, so much so that I saw no one following those men or walking behind them; instead, people flocked to Abd al-Rahman and consulted him during those nights. When the night came before the morning on which we pledged allegiance to Uthman, Abd al-Rahman came to me after part of the night had passed and knocked until I awoke. He said, “I see you are sleeping. By Allah, I have hardly slept at all tonight. Go and call al-Zubayr and Sad.” I called them, and he consulted them. Then he called me and said, “Call Ali.” I called him, and Abd al-Rahman spoke privately with him until the night was very late. Ali then left, still hopeful, though Abd al-Rahman had some concern about Ali. Then Abd al-Rahman said, “Call Uthman.” I called him, and he spoke privately with him until the dawn caller separated them. After Abd al-Rahman led the people in the dawn prayer, the appointed group gathered by the pulpit. He sent for the Emigrants and Ansar who were present and for the commanders of the armies who had come on that pilgrimage with Umar. When they had assembled, Abd al-Rahman testified and said: “Now then, Ali, I have considered the people’s affairs and have not seen them prefer anyone over Uthman. Do not create a way against yourself.” Ali said: “I pledge allegiance to you on the basis of the Sunnah of Allah and His Messenger and the two caliphs after him.” Abd al-Rahman pledged allegiance to him, and the Emigrants, Ansar, army commanders, and Muslims pledged allegiance.
